one_sentence: The Grace Operator G, a non-unitary idempotent projection, structurally models prevenient grace as an external, irreversible sign-flip from fallen to redeemed.
executive_summary: This document formalizes the doctrine of prevenient grace using non-unitary operator algebra. The Grace Operator G acts on a two-state Hilbert space, mapping both |+1> and |-1> to |+1>, satisfying idempotency (G²=G) and non-unitarity (G†G≠I). Key properties—externality, completeness in one application, irreversibility, and voluntary reception—map to theological claims: grace originates outside the system (Ephesians 2:8-9), is once-for-all (Hebrews 10:14), and irrevocable (Romans 11:29). The mapping is partially reverse-engineered from theology, but gains independent support from ISO-002's impossibility theorems and yields falsifiable predictions, such as the impossibility of self-generated grace. The document concludes that justification (idempotent G) and sanctification (unitary S(t)) are distinct operators, reinforcing sola gratia.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism record (ISO-013) mapping the Grace Operator G from non-unitary operator algebra to the Christian doctrine of prevenient grace. The core structural claim is that G is an idempotent, non-unitary, rank-1 projection that maps all input states to a single positive output, mirroring grace's externality, sufficiency, and irreversibility. Key evidence includes the mathematical properties of G (G²=G, det(G)=0) and theological references (Ephesians 2:8-9, Hebrews 10:14, Romans 11:29), supported by ISO-002's impossibility theorems. This matters because it provides a rigorous formal framework for grace, distinguishing justification from sanctification and ruling out Pelagianism via operator algebra.
